pattern_title: Authorization classification and unmapped facility shifts need validation before action
pattern_description: A large share of the identified increase is tied to authorization-classification movement rather than a clean utilization or price story. FL, CA, and IN / MD / MO all show the same authorization distribution issue, and IA adds a separate facility mapping problem through a Not Mapped bucket. These items should be treated as gating validation work before changing UM, reimbursement, or network strategy.

claims.summary: FL authorization classification shifts account for about $58.1M and are flagged for validation before action. CA shows another $18.3M with the same authorization classification issue, centered in neurologic and back-related inpatient cases. IN / MD / MO add about $12.6M, including Riley's Children's Health and delivery and behavioral health cases. IA adds about $3.4M in LTSS Dual Eligible spend tied to a Not Mapped facility bucket and no-auth claims, indicating a separate mapping problem.

pattern_title: FL free-standing SNF growth is the largest real utilization driver
pattern_description: FL free-standing SNF spend rose sharply, driven mainly by more admissions rather than a broad spike in unit prices. The increase is concentrated in LTSS Dual Eligible members, with additional growth in LTSS Non Dual. Neurologic and back-related cases appear repeatedly, so the business lever is tighter control of SNF entry, stay management, and discharge planning.

claims.summary: FL LTSS Dual Eligible free-standing SNFs added about $61.3M, including 6,568 more admissions and 10,981 more claims. FL LTSS Non Dual free-standing SNFs added about $8.1M with 853 more admissions. A smaller but related FL SNF pressure point added about $1.1M in Medical Back Problems without MCC, showing some added unit-cost pressure inside the larger volume story.

pattern_title: CA nursing-facility and SNF growth is concentrated in neuro and spine cases
pattern_description: CA shows a focused nursing-facility story rather than broad inpatient inflation. Clinical NF growth is concentrated in neurologic, stroke-sequelae, and spine-related cases, while operational SNF growth appears across LTSS Dual Eligible, LTSS Non Dual, and TANF Standard products. Operational paid per admit is often flat or down, which reinforces that more case flow and case mix are the main drivers.

claims.summary: CA NF clinical case mix added about $11.6M, led by stroke sequelae, spinal stenosis, radiculopathy, Parkinson disease, and Alzheimer's disease. CA LTSS Dual Eligible free-standing SNFs added about $6.0M with 509 more admissions while paid per admit was slightly down. CA LTSS Non Dual free-standing SNFs added about $4.9M with 464 more admissions and lower paid per admit, again pointing to volume over price. CA TANF Standard free-standing SNFs added about $1.9M with 192 more admissions.

pattern_title: Tampa General is a concentrated FL acute-hospital cost driver
pattern_description: FL acute-hospital cost pressure is concentrated at Tampa General Hospital, especially in ABD Non Dual members. The pattern includes both higher admission volume and meaningful paid-per-admission increases, which makes this more than a simple utilization issue. A smaller NICU concentration adds additional high-cost intensity at the same provider.

claims.summary: FL ABD Non Dual acute hospitals added about $5.9M with 422 more admissions. Tampa General Hospital added about $2.2M of ABD Non Dual acute-hospital spend with only 27 more admissions, implying roughly $9.9K higher paid per admit. Tampa General TANF Standard acute-hospital cases added about $336K through 63 more admissions. A smaller Tampa General NICU concentration added about $547K across 3 admissions, with about $103.6K higher paid per admit.

pattern_title: Riley's Children's Health is the main IN provider concentration
pattern_description: Indiana children's spend is highly concentrated at Riley's Children's Health across more than one Medicaid product. The largest block is TANF Standard, where both admissions and paid per admission increased, with a smaller but similar pattern in Family Care. This is a provider economics issue first, with UM review needed alongside any reimbursement action.

claims.summary: Riley's Children's Health drove about $7.3M in IN TANF Standard children's facility spend, with 99 more admissions and about $4.9K higher paid per admit. IN Family Care children's facility added about $1.0M at the same provider, with 19 more admissions and about $2.9K higher paid per admit.

pattern_title: NC behavioral health and acute psych spend is rising on both volume and intensity
pattern_description: North Carolina behavioral health costs increased through a combination of more admissions and materially higher paid per admission. The operational pressure is centered in acute psych for TANF Foster Care, while the clinical side is concentrated in PTSD, adjustment disorder, and stress-related inpatient behavioral health cases. A small rare-case component is also present, so some of the increase is volatile even though the broader trend is real.

claims.summary: NC TANF Foster Care acute psych added about $1.9M with 46 more admissions and roughly $41.2K higher paid per admit. NC IP BH cases for PTSD and adjustment disorder added about $1.5M with 53 more admissions combined and paid per admit up roughly $7.6K to $19.1K. Rare stress and OCD behavioral health cases added another about $488K on just 12 admissions, making part of the signal small-N and volatile.

pattern_title: Maternity delivery episodes show focused pressure across several states
pattern_description: Delivery-related spend is showing a focused cross-state pattern rather than broad hospital inflation. Maryland has the clearest clinical concentration through obstetric complications and higher-paid delivery episodes, while MD, IN, NY, KS, and MO also show acute-hospital delivery pressure tied to vaginal delivery cases with O.R. procedures. The common business lever is maternity episode management and payment logic review.

claims.summary: MD obstetric delivery and newborn cases added about $572K, led by post-term pregnancy and severe pre-eclampsia, with paid per admit up about $4.1K and $3.1K. Acute-hospital delivery episodes also rose in MD ($335K), IN ($295K), NY ($345K), KS ($258K), and MO ($246K). The recurring driver was vaginal delivery with O.R. procedures, pointing to a focused maternity episode pattern.

pattern_title: Behavioral health pressure extends into MO and smaller acute-psych markets
pattern_description: Missouri shows a meaningful behavioral health pattern across both clinical IP BH cases and acute-hospital operational spend, especially depressive and other neuroses. Smaller but similar acute-psych increases are also present in NY and WV, where higher paid per admit is part of the story. Together, these indicate broader behavioral health pressure outside North Carolina, though at lower scale.

claims.summary: MO IP BH cases for major depression and unspecified depression added about $1.6M with 100 more admissions combined and paid per admit up about $4.1K to $4.6K. MO acute-hospital behavioral health cases added about $1.3M, led by depressive and other neuroses with 84 more admissions and roughly $1.9K to $2.9K higher paid per admit. Smaller acute-psych spikes also appeared in NY ($451K) and WV ($408K), both tied to depressive episodes and higher paid per admit.
